question.text: A strategic sale as an AIF exit involves:

answer.text: Selling units on the stock exchange
Selling the investee company stake to a corporate buyer in the same or related industry
The fund manager buying the investment personally

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook (p.218) describes a strategic sale or M&A exit as similar to a secondary sale, except that the buyer is a corporate buyer in the same industry — or a larger company seeking entry into that industry. The strategic nature of the buyer is what distinguishes this route from a pure financial-investor secondary. The Trap: Selling AIF units on the stock exchange is not how a PE/VC AIF exits an investee. The fund manager buying personally would be a conflicted related-party transaction, and returning unsold investments in specie is a distribution-in-kind, not a strategic sale. Note: Source reference: NISM Series XIX-A workbook p.218 (strategic sale / M&A exit — corporate buyer in the same or related industry).
